## One-line Summary

Continual Harness edits prompts, subagents, skills, and memory during a continuous episode, with a separate teacher-assisted model/harness co-learning experiment.

## 1. Document Information

Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents. 2605.09998v1; first submitted 2026/05/11. The exact [local PDF](../papers/karten-2026-continual-harness-online-adaptation-for.pdf) has 28 pages. Citations use 1-based PDF pages. Review covers the main method, cited experiments and limitations; no reproduction was run. [Author-linked project/code](https://sethkarten.ai/continual-harness) is provided for follow-up; implementation behavior was not audited. The PDF-supplied project page returned HTTP 403 during this scan.

## 2. Key Contributions

Makes reset-free adaptation the unit of study: the environment continues while reusable agent components change. Distinguishes the automated framework from earlier Gemini Plays Pokemon runs that mixed human and agent refinement. [PDF p. 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=3) [PDF p. 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=4) [PDF p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=6)

## 3. Methodology and Architecture

After warm-up, a refiner periodically reads a trajectory window and edits four harness components via fixed meta-tools. The acting and refining roles share a model in the main experiments. A separate co-learning loop uses 256-step live rollouts, process-reward scoring, teacher relabeling of low-reward windows, and soft SFT updates while preserving emulator state. This is not the same training objective as CoSkill joint role RL. [PDF p. 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=4) [PDF p. 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=5) [PDF p. 8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=8)

## 4. Key Results and Benchmarks

For the Pro model on Emerald, Section 4.4 reports a $130 median cost at 100% of the monitored milestones from scratch, versus $215 at 98% for the minimalist baseline. These are paper-era API costs and the specified milestone set, not full-game completion costs. Flash-Lite reverses the benefit: the minimalist setup reaches 20%, while Continual Harness variants reach 3-13% at comparable or higher cost. The study reports at least three seeds and seed medians. [PDF p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=6) [PDF p. 7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=7) [PDF p. 8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=8)

## 5. Limitations and Future Work

A single episode advancing across training iterations does not establish independent held-out improvement. Human-assisted historical game completions should not be attributed to the fully automated method. Benefits depend strongly on the base model. Model/harness co-learning also depends on supervised warm-up and a stronger teacher, and the experiments remain within Pokemon environments. [PDF p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=6) [PDF p. 7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=7) [PDF p. 8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09998v1#page=8)

## 6. Related Work

[[hebbar-2026-sia-self-improving-ai]]; [[karten-2026-prime-agent-a-self-improving]]. Synthesis: [[concepts/procedural-self-improvement]] and [[overviews/self-improving-llm-agents]].

## 7. Glossary

Reset-free: preserve environment state across updates. Refiner: model role that edits reusable harness state. DAgger-style relabeling: teacher correction of learner-visited states.
